records.distractors: 1/4 s confuses τ² with duration;2 s inverts the mass-to-stiffness ratio. π s is full T, not τ. The negative root is not a physical duration.
records.manualArithmetic: Mass 1 kg divided by stiffness 4 N/m is 1/4 s². Its positive root is τ=1/2 s; the complete period is T=π s.
records.physicalAssumptions: Horizontal ideal massless spring and constant positive inertial mass, frictionless support, vertical weight and normal balanced. Linear elastic regime around stable equilibrium, no damping or driving. τ is T/(2π), never full T, with positive duration and positive stiffness. Parameters may vary between trials, remain constant during each oscillation. Display readings are continuous dimensionless values.

source.reference: Apply Newton to a horizontal ideal linear spring: x″+(k/m)x=0. Derive ω²=k/m and τ=1/ω=T/(2π), keeping full period, reduced period, frequency and positive roots distinct.
